newsitem.title: USA: US starts evacuation of Americans from Albania.
newsitem.headline: US starts evacuation of Americans from Albania.

text.p: The United States has begun a military evacuation from Albania of non-essential U.S. embassy employees as well as all other Americans who wish to leave, the State Department said on Thursday.

State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said four U.S. military helicopters had landed in Tirana in the last few hours to start the evacuation. He said there was a breakdown in public order and added: "We believe the situation will continue to deteriorate."

Burns told a news conference: "Just in the last hour four Chinook 46 helicopters landed in Tirana. These helicopters were from our fleet in the Ionian Sea ... They discharged some forward deployed elements of a small group of forces that will assist in the United States evacuation from Albania."

Burns said about 50 Americans, most of them children, had already been brought out of the violence-wracked Balkan country to U.S. ships standing offshore. "We're going to be continuing this operation over the course of the next several hours and perhaps the next several days," he said.

He said about 170 non-essential embassy employees and their dependents as well as some 2,000 other Americans were eligible for evacuation. The ambassador and other key staff members would not be leaving at this stage, he said.
He said the United States was coordinating its evacuation with other NATO allies and U.S. forces would also bring out other foreigners who needed to leave where necessary.
